interface_detail: probe hardware or software probe; REST API for measurements
limits_note: Hosting a probe earns credits, and credits buy measurements - not bytes and not disk. A software probe can run on your own infrastructure, which makes it the most accessible thing in this whole slot (no shipping, no institution), but it is a measurement vantage point with trivial bandwidth and no storage. Anchors are bigger and require a datacentre-grade commitment plus approval.
reliability_note: Hardware probes are frequently out of stock; software probes have negligible throughput by design.

extras.interface_verbatim: probe hardware or software probe; REST API for measurements
extras.agent_focus: Marketplaces and networks where storage or bandwidth is contributed by third parties for free or near-free. Two directions probed: (1) BUY side - can you consume contributed bandwidth/storage cheaply; (2) SUPPLY side - the arbitrage question, whether contributing a disk earns storage credit at better than the retail rate. Also research testbeds that hand out whole physical nodes with multi-TB local disk (CloudLab, Chameleon, FABRIC, Emulab) and community mesh networks (Guifi, Freifunk, NYC Mesh). Decided per candidate by computing 20 TiB stored + 1 TiB/day egress against that path's actual tariff.
